clue.text: Painting gives some amusement over in the Far East

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for a place found there

indicators.note: turned over, the whole string is read from its far end back
only some of the following word is wanted, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: painting is an art
taken as written, then cut to its first four letters

explanation.surface: An oriental painting provides a little entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: ART followed by AMUS (some of amusement) gives ARTAMUS, and the whole run backwards is SUMATRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Indonesian island lies in south-east Asia, loosely counted as part of the Orient by the setter.

clue.text: Monkey taken in by contemptible character's fraud

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible person
a monkey is slang for five hundred pounds; D is the Roman numeral for 500, with L tacked on

explanation.surface: A monkey is grabbed by some nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a monkey is £500, which is D in Roman numerals; the extra L (50) is not clearly accounted for by the clue, so the setter seems to stretch the monkey to DL.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a deception practised to cheat someone out of money, which is exactly what a fraud is.

clue.text: Menace nude girls constitute for opposite sex?

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are made up into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Threatening naked girls make up the other sex, a cheeky picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition only works relative to the girls of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative to girls, the opposite sex is male, and masculine gender is the grammatical or general term for male.

clue.text: When it's over, redhead shows fatigue

indicators.note: turned over, the little word preceding it is read backwards

parts.note: the word it, turned round
split as red plus head, and a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Once it is all finished, a ginger-haired person looks worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Redhead must be split: red is taken literally, and head becomes a geographical term for a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and fatigue are both names for the weary state of exhaustion after effort.

clue.text: Tree that makes a student swot

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, a student
to mug up is to swot, study hard

explanation.surface: A wooden object that turns a student into a bookworm.
explanation.walkthrough: To swot and to mug (up) are British for cramming for an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Almug is a biblical tree whose valuable wood was brought to Solomon, mentioned in the Book of Kings.

clue.text: Church lists included in purge

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it, so it goes in the middle

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A church roll-call figures in an expulsion of members.
explanation.walkthrough: Lists looks like a noun (registers) but is the verb for tilting, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purge: rid something of impurities or undesirable elements.

clue.text: One solicits container savers for recycling

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: material sent for recycling is broken down and remade, so the word is reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A collector goes round asking people to hand in containers for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes door to door seeking votes or orders, so is someone who solicits support.

clue.text: Marriage guidance can't begin to raise one's spirit…

indicators.note: unable to begin means the opening letter of the name is lost

parts.note: Relate is the British relationship-counselling charity, formerly Marriage Guidance

explanation.surface: Couples counselling fails to cheer anyone up, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate is the UK charity that offers marriage counselling; it was once called the Marriage Guidance Council.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to make them very happy, lifting their mood and morale.

clue.text: … community spirit exhibited in soap script

indicators.note: something exhibited in a frame is shown inside it, so it goes within the other word

parts.note: Neighbours is the long-running Australian TV soap opera, hugely popular in Britain
an actor's script is their lines

explanation.surface: Friendly community feeling is on show in a television drama's script.
explanation.walkthrough: The script goes inside the soap's title, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbourliness is friendly helpfulness among people living nearby, the essence of community spirit.

clue.text: Linette's new style

indicators.note: a new version of the name is made by rearranging its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Linette has a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: Style looks like a noun (her new style) but is the verb meaning to give a title to.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to call them by a particular title, which is what entitle means in its naming sense.

clue.text: One's line is broadcast art — must listen in

definitions.note: short for one whose line (of music) it is

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's lines go out on the radio, and art lovers are urged to tune in.
explanation.walkthrough: Line here is both a line of work and a musical line played by one performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a musician whose part, or line, in a piece is played on an instrument.

clue.text: Old priest managed without sport

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: managed, as in coped or did
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: An ancient cleric got by without games.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like lacking, but here means outside, so the sport is enclosed rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were the priests of the ancient Celtic religion in Britain, Ireland and Gaul.

clue.text: Fruit stolen and loaded for wide distribution

definitions.note: describes what the shot is used for, a noun

parts.note: grapes are fruit
hot goods are stolen ones

explanation.surface: Stolen fruit is piled up for sale far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded suggests goods on a lorry, but it means loaded into a cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon so that they scatter widely.

clue.text: Prime side dressed in its own wrapping?

indicators.note: food that is dressed is prepared and rearranged, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime cut of meat is served in its natural covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, the covering a body comes wrapped in by nature.

clue.text: Angel made unusual appearance for Mary

indicators.note: the words appear in an unusual form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angel appeared strangely to the Virgin Mary, like an Annunciation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Virgin, but the answer is the other Mary of the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus, so her surname-like title identifies a particular Mary.

clue.text: Milton set old books in order

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so one piece is lodged within the other

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
OT is the Old Testament, a set of old books

explanation.surface: A poet arranges ancient volumes in a tidy sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton suggests the English poet, but it is Milton Obote, first prime minister and later president of Uganda; in order reads as tidily but is the container's host.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Obote led Uganda after independence, so his first name is enough to point to the surname.

clue.text: There's nothing squalid out east working in a harem

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, the answer is a noun

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: out as in put out of order, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
E for east

explanation.surface: Life in an eastern harem is presented as far from sordid.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or concubine serving in a Turkish sultan's household.

clue.text: Chance of getting results, lacking time?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: results of a match or race are its events' outcomes
T for time

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders about the odds of results arriving without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Results here are events, as in the outcomes listed on a race card.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is betting odds of one to one, a fifty-fifty chance of winning.

clue.text: Imprisoned unmelodic composer in the finish

indicators.note: the composer is placed in the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: the finish is the end
John Cage wrote experimental, tuneless music such as 4'33"

explanation.surface: A tuneless composer was locked up at the end of his life.
explanation.definitionFit: To be encaged is to be shut in a cage, a vivid synonym for imprisoned or confined.

clue.text: Spice girl takes less than a flash to get past it

indicators.note: less than the whole phrase means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice of the pop group the Spice Girls
a trice is a flash, an instant

explanation.surface: A pop star is over the hill in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Spice girl looks like a name for a woman who sells spices, but points to the 1990s pop band.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is informal for too old to function well, which geriatric is used to mean colloquially.

clue.text: Revolutionary gets down under on a solo passage

parts.note: Jack Cade led the rebellion of 1450 in Kent
New Zealand is part of the region called down under
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel heads off to Australasia on a lone trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is an ornamental solo passage for the soloist in a concerto, often improvised.

clue.text: To spy on one's partner is the end

parts.note: to check on someone is to spy on them
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Keeping tabs on your spouse spells the death of the relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate ends a game of chess, and figuratively means utter defeat, the finish.

clue.text: Private cover?

parts.note: surface reading: something that hides personal matters, as in a cover for privacy
setter's reading: what a private soldier is clothed in, the uniform colour and cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Private is a soldier of the lowest rank, and cover is clothing; the brownish-green uniform cloth is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the drab dull-coloured cloth used for army uniforms, so it covers a private soldier.

clue.text: Guidelines for conduct in the thick of battle

indicators.note: the letters sit in the following words, straddling their join

parts.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding completing the familiar phrase

explanation.surface: Rules of behaviour applying in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Of battle is pure surface, finishing the familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles governing how people should behave.

clue.text: Saga reflected in the Mirror and other dailies

parts.note: surface padding: the Mirror is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters appear back to front
the letters are lodged inside the newspaper word at the end

parts.note: the run of letters at the end of the word, before it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A long story is reported in a tabloid and its rival newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British daily newspaper, so the surface is about press coverage, while reflected supplies the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is an epic poem of the Trojan War, a heroic saga in verse.

clue.text: A standing item for many a public function

definitions.text: A standing item for many a public function

parts.words: A standing item for many a public function
parts.note: surface reading: a regular agenda entry on the programme of formal events

parts.words: A standing item for many a public function
parts.note: setter's reading: something the audience stands up for, the anthem played at official occasions

explanation.walkthrough: Standing item sounds like committee jargon, but the audience literally stands for the British national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national anthem is traditionally played at official events, with everyone rising to their feet.

clue.text: Animals find lack of warmth in their sleeping quarters

parts.note: short for dormitory
ice is the absence of heat

explanation.surface: Creatures discover their bedroom is freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: the quarters first, then the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small hibernating rodents, so they qualify as animals by example.

clue.text: The young Clinton could be a pensioner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the daughter of Bill and Hillary Clinton

definitions.note: describes a pensioner of that name, not the word itself
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a retired soldier at the Royal Hospital in London is called by this name

explanation.surface: The President's daughter might one day be drawing a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea pensioner is a retired British soldier living at the Royal Hospital Chelsea, famous for scarlet coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is the Clintons' daughter, and also the London district whose veteran residents are known by that name.
